This plant grows as a full bush in areas with sandy soil.

I discovered this plant in South America

It likes lots of sun and little water.

It is not only pest resistant but its fragrant showy flowers also attract a great many beneficial insects.

As the name suggests, young flower buds can be pickled and make a wonderful caper like condiment. They are wonderful with fish or seafood. Lots of people who I have fed them to could not tell the difference.

After the showy flowers fall off, a small beans is produced. The beans will ripen and twist open [revealing a bright red interior and white seed coat]http://www.cnip.org.br/PFNMs/img/img_feijao/02_grande.jpg). This makes it one of the nicest edible ornamental tree to have if climate permits. For those in colder regions, it can be made into a wonderful house plant, as long as you provide with a good sized pot and lots of sunshine.

The bean (once the white pulp removed) can be dried for 2 days and replanted to make more babies. It is a perennial so it will give you a bounty of beans that have a VERY special taste, that of Wasabi!

Yes, this bean can be processed with a little oil to make a very nice Wasabi.

Now you must remember that all wasabi that you eat in American sushi restaurants is actually mustard oil!

If you can find some mustard oil, then you can make a very spicy and quite unique Wasabi.

This is a great plant for people in Zone 7 and up ;-)
